items.gist: The bhuvarloka lies one lakh from the sun, with ten wind paths spaced ten thousand apart; the first is Ritariddhi.
Successive cloud layers rain on beings, while Vinayakas born of Mahadeva destroy the karma of the unrefined.
The Vajranka wind holds lower Vidyadharas and those who died attaining siddhis through vidya or cremation rites.
The Vaidyuta wind contains clouds, apsaras, meritorious humans, and those who died in fire, water, battle, or rescue.
The Raivata wind carries nourishing and disease-clouds, while Visavarta is the wind of wrathful waters.
Above it are storm clouds, special Vidyadharas, and worshippers of Parameshvara; beyond lies Durjaya.
Paravaha, Avaha, Mahavaha, and Mahaparivaha contain Brahma clouds, Vidyadharas, and Matrs under Rudra's power.
The second path and beyond contain Siddhas, Caranas, divine weapons, elephants, Garuda, Ganga, Bull, Daksha, Vasus, Rudras, Adityas, and the sun's mandala.
Svarloka extends to Dhruva; the moon, nakshatras, Saptarshis, and Dhruva are described as powers and stations.
Beings are bound in the nilamandala; after sacrifice without knowledge they go to heaven, then return to human birth.
Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, and Satyaloka contain sages, deities, Kapila, Sanaka, and Brahma revealing the universe.
Above are Ananda, Vishnu's city, and Rudra's cities; Rudra grants liberation and moksha by Shiva's will.
Seven worlds are gross, while subtler worlds are covered by tanmatras and mahabhutas.
The cosmic egg, brahmanda, and surrounding hundred Rudras are described as the support of the universe.
The text distinguishes vastupinda from anda through Shakti, unity, and non-separation in tattvas.
The guna-tanmatra mass is the anda; the hundred Rudras have eleven great lords, ending with Ananta, Kapali, Agni, Yama, Nirrti, and Bala.
